stepAnswer: glucose uptake by cells and glycogen storage
cells take up glucose and liver stores glycogen
stepExplanation: Insulin has two main effects: (1) It increases glucose uptake by body cells (especially muscle and fat cells), and (2) it stimulates the liver to convert excess glucose to **glycogen** for storage. This is negative feedback because lowered glucose inhibits further insulin release.
stepBody: How does insulin lower blood glucose levels? Describe what happens to glucose in target cells and the liver.
